subject: getting the state/range probabilities at each node

messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: getting the state/range probabilities at each node
parts:
Answer to a question:

Nicholas – we're having difficulty making publication-quality figures from the BioGeoBEARS output.  Because the pie charts seems to be raster based rather than vector based, it takes forever (for our purposes, at least) to rotate figures in Illustrator, and there doesn't seem to be any reliable way to select or unselect all the lines.  Is there a way of getting the %'s for each pie diagram, so that we can re-draw them ourselves?  With nine ancestral areas, there are just far, far too many options to provide a color key, and we'd like to replace the unlikely possibilities by a uniform light grey.  Thanks for any suggestions or help!  Cheers, [redacted]

Hi!

Yeah, this is a common question.

Answers:

1. You can get the state probabilities numbers from the results object as follows: https://groups.google.com/d/msg/biogeobears/eGzLRPg10y0/5DQZBqXbME8J

2. This gives you a table where the columns are the states (the possible ranges), and the rows are the nodes (including tips).

3. To get the node numbers for all nodes in the tree etc., use the prt() function (print tree).

4. To get the names of the states/ranges: https://groups.google.com/d/msg/biogeobears/1wyy3jV2gDs/wUodaUSHb0YJ

Finally, if you have a lot of areas and little resolution, displaying probabilities by area rather than by range can be useful. I've got some code for that somewhere, I'm not sure if its online, one of the functions is infprobs_to_probs_of_each_area_from_relprobs(), email me next week at mat...@nimbios.org and I could dig up a script if you want to pursue that.

Cheers,
Nick

I use Inkscape to edit the PDF output files from BioGeoBEARS.  Pie charts with at least two colors will display properly in Inkscape, but not the single-colored ones. You can also rotate the tree or edit the branches. Inkscape is similar to CorelDraw, but it is free.
